The notion that people have to move out of their parents' house to be taken seriously is largely an American construct, and there are many major cultures that traditionally live in family houses containing potentially four or more generations.

There are several reasons that actually make living with your parents a good idea, and the upward trend of US children living with their parents for longer is indicative of this. The main reason is financial; obviously, it's much easier to sustain yourself, even if you're paying your parents fair-rent for accommodating you once you start working, and that money will eventually come back to you in some way, anyways. Other reasons can include security (outside forces, illnesses, car trouble, etc.), easy division of chores or tasks that increases efficiency for individuals, and simply having an easily accessible face-to-face form of socialization.

I'm more or less reconciled to the thought of taking care of my parents and the household once they're too old, as well. If and when I do marry and have children of my own, having my parents live with me grants the added benefits of 24/7 daycare services.
